subject: Provisional isolate + compatibility gate for harpoon-lite variant
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, ingest-support@forgeai.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New variant intake: harpoon-lite (provisional isolate request)

Hi team,

Quick ask: ForgeAI sent over a new 6B variant they call "harpoon-lite". Their repo snapshot flagged a tokenizer change (see attached PDF) that could produce tokenization mismatches with our current harpoon-v1 family. Given the potential for split/merge differences on prefix caching, I want to request a provisional isolate + compatibility gate for this variant while we validate behavior end-to-end.

Scope I want covered:
- Temporary routing of harpoon-lite traffic to isolated staging pool (no live routing)
- Tokenization parity tests against our customer canonical prompts (attached sample set)
- Canary runbook (small % traffic) if parity looks good — we should define rollback windows
- Telemetry flags to watch: prefix cache hit-rate, token delta ratio, latency p50/p95 change, and generation divergence on our eval prompts

Timeline: Forge wants intake next week (their ask is 7/5). If we can't meet that, we should provide a clear blocked-by list to them.

Attachments: harpoon-lite_tokenizer-diff.pdf, harpoon-lite-sample-prompts.json

Can Priyom/David weigh in on the technical risk and whether we can stage this as a provisional isolate? Also tagging ingest-support@forgeai.com so they can send any missing artifacts (tokenizer files, vocabulary maps).

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Model Intake
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, ingest-support@forgeai.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New variant intake: harpoon-lite (provisional isolate request)

Thanks Lauren — good flags. Quick notes from Applied ML:

1) Tokenizer diffs alone can be survivable if we map token ids, but we need the exact tokenizer binary / config (BPE merges, special tokens). If Forge can provide the tokenizer wheel or a deterministic tokenizer test harness that would speed things.
2) We should run prompt-level regression tests (over our evaluation set) and compute token-by-token edit distance and LM-logp delta. If the logp shift is > 0.5 on mean across critical prompts, we should hold.
3) For fallback, plan should be: live requests go to harpoon-v1; if canary looks good after 24h and telemetry is nominal, we can promote.

I can author the eval harness and run the stat tests, but I'll need a dedicated staging pool to ensure cache isolation. Tessa — can you confirm capacity for a provisional pool?

Priyom
Priyom Das
Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, ingest-support@forgeai.com, Beth Carlson <beth@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New variant intake: harpoon-lite (provisional isolate request)

+1 on the provisional isolate. David — can infra spin up a small staging pool (2 GPU nodes) isolated from prefix caches and routing? We need:
- no cross-pool KV cache sharing
- separate model variant tag so we can route test traffic and optionally a 1% canary if we flip the flag later
- ability to snapshot kernel selection logs for quantization/compilation checks

David, prioritize a checklist: kernel support (A100/80GB), quantization path readiness (q4/q8), and whether sequence-length pathing differs for this model. Priyom, once pool exists, drop your harness and I'll coordinate scheduling with Forge.

Forge ingest-support — please confirm you can provide the tokenizer binary and the model's compile artifact. Beth (ACME), fyi — you expressed interest in harpoon-lite in the outbound summit; if you'd like I can loop you into the canary plan later.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Dedicated Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ingest-support@forgeai.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New variant intake: harpoon-lite (provisional isolate request)

On Thu, Jul 1, 2027 at 09:47 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> +1 on the provisional isolate. David — can infra spin up a small staging pool (2 GPU nodes) isolated from prefix caches and routing?

We can do the staging pool. Plan and ETA:
- Provisioning: 2x A100-80GB nodes in us-west-2, isolated tenant network, estimated 4h to carve and configure.
- KV-cache isolation: will disable cross-pool KV propagation and create an ephemeral cache namespace tied to the variant tag.
- Kernel/quantization: harpoon-lite artifacts show mixed int8 kernels; we'll run a quick compile to check for missing ops. If any kernel fallback is required, compilation could add 6-12h.
- Canary wiring: we'll create a feature-flagged route and a 1% split target for a 24h canary window. Rollback is immediate (flip route back to harpoon-v1).
- Telemetry: set alerts on prefix cache drop >10%, token-delta ratio >0.1, latency p95 increase >15%, and generation divergence >0.08 (we'll produce baseline numbers).

Need from Forge: tokenizer wheel + model compile artifact + a short README of any custom ops. Forge, can you send by EOD Monday (7/5)? If we get everything Monday morning we can aim for a canary by Tuesday.

Attachment: canary-runbook.md (initial draft)

-David
David Kim
SRE Lead, Serving Infra
Redwood Inference
